doc.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

chapter: Founding the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band
title: House parties and founding the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band in 1973
summary: From parties at his big Long Island Sound house, he and Clyde Bernhardt agreed to form a band, which first toured Scandinavia in 1976.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: How did the initial idea, was it 1973?

Well how it started was that the orthodontic practice I started in ’61 became successful and we bought a big house down on the Long Island Sound, 18-room Tudor house, and there were only three of us in it — my wife, my daughter and myself. And we could have a hundred people. And by that time I’d gotten to know quite a few jazz musicians and we decided to have some parties. And they were unusual parties because everybody brought a dish of some kind and we had probably a preponderance of black musicians, although there were quite a few whites. And some of these black ladies can really cook. So we supplied the chairs, the cups, and we had party people come and help us with chairs and all of that kind of stuff. But these parties, they got to be — people looked forward to them. It was great. I mean here I’ve got J.C. Higginbotham playing in my dining room. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

You know? It was a dream come true. And so at one point I got to know Clyde Bernhardt and so on March 5th or March 3rd, 1973, at one of the parties, in a rash moment I said to Clyde, “We ought to form a band.” And he said, “Well okay, if you’ll take care of most of the business part, you know, I’ll certainly go along.” So that’s how the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band formed. From these parties. And this was 1973 and we made our first trip to Scandinavia in ’76. Now I was in my 40s and the guys were all in their 60s.
